title: Effective Field Theory of Operator Scrambling from Strong-to-Weak Symmetry Breaking
authors: Bai-Lin Cheng, Shao-Kai Jian, Zhi-Cheng Yang
abstract: Operator scrambling is commonly diagnosed by the growth of out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs), yet a general symmetry principle underlying their effective dynamics has remained elusive. For Brownian or short-time-correlated large-$N$ Majorana systems, we develop a symmetry-based effective field theory for operator scrambling, organized by a strong-to-weak U(1) symmetry breaking in operator space. The key observation is that, in the noninteracting fermion limit, the four-fold Keldysh contour representation of an OTOC admits an emergent strong U(1) symmetry in a doubled Hilbert-space description, even when the original system has no ordinary conserved quantity. The associated slow mode is the phase of the strong-charge creation operator, whose conjugate density is identified with the local operator size. Generic interactions explicitly break the strong symmetry and generate a mass term at lowest order for the would-be Goldstone mode, thereby converting diffusive operator spreading into chaotic growth. We further show that higher-order symmetry breaking terms are tightly constrained by an emergent duality that combines time reversal with contour permutation. This duality fixes the effective action up to quadratic order in the response field, relates the multiplicative noise strength directly to the Lyapunov exponent, and makes the positivity of the Lyapunov exponent a consequence of convergence of the real-time path integral. The resulting OTOC dynamics is governed by a noisy FKPP equation, which captures within a unified framework the early-time exponential growth, ballistic propagation, nonlinear saturation, and stochastic front broadening of operator scrambling. We verify this construction in a Brownian SYK chain, where a direct saddle-point expansion reproduces the symmetry-based effective action. Our results reveal a symmetry origin of operator-size hydrodynamics and scrambling.
summary: The paper develops an Effective Field Theory to explain operator scrambling using Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs). By identifying an emergent strong U(1) symmetry in the doubled Hilbert space, the authors derive that the dynamics must follow a noisy FKPP equation. This provides a unified, symmetry-based understanding of how quantum information spreads and thermalizes in complex many-body systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is to find a general symmetry principle that governs the effective dynamics of operator scrambling, which is diagnosed by Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs). The challenge lies in developing an Effective Field Theory (EFT) for this process.
main_result: The OTOC dynamics are shown to be governed by a noisy FKPP equation, derived from an EFT built upon the spontaneous breaking of an emergent strong U(1) symmetry. This framework unifies descriptions of early-time exponential growth and late-time saturation in operator spreading.
method: The authors develop a symmetry-based Effective Field Theory (EFT) by mapping the four-fold Keldysh contour representation of the OTOC onto a doubled Hilbert space, allowing for systematic analysis via slow modes and emergent symmetries.
model_or_system: The theory is developed for Majorana systems (specifically Brownian or short-time-correlated large-N Majorana systems). A key test case used to verify the construction is the Brownian Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) chain.
key_observables: Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators (OTOCs), operator size ($N[O(t)]$), and the resulting dynamics described by a noisy FKPP equation.
important_parameters: The analysis involves organizing terms based on strong-to-weak U(1) symmetry breaking, and key parameters include the Lyapunov exponent ($\lambda_L$) which is directly related to the noise strength.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on systematic expansions in powers of the slow mode field $\phi$, assuming consistency with Schwinger-Keldysh conditions, and imposing constraints like an emergent duality combining time reversal and contour permutation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates a mathematical mapping from a four-fold Keldysh contour integral to a standard two-segment contour in a doubled Hilbert space, which is crucial for the EFT construction.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem using OTOCs and introduces the symmetry-based EFT framework. It then derives the effective action by exploiting emergent symmetries (U(1) breaking), leading to the noisy FKPP equation. Finally, it verifies this structure using a specific model like the Brownian SYK chain.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general theoretical tool—an EFT derived from symmetry principles—to describe non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly interacting quantum systems, which is highly relevant for understanding thermalization and chaos in many-body physics.

(b) In the doubled Hilbert space H2, this four-fold contour is reduced to a standard two-fold contour. The OTOC is equivalent to the expectation value of the occupation-number operator Nx,j(t) in the state |O⟩≡(OL ⊗IR)|0⟩. (c) The system can be further mapped to a single directed path in the quadrupled Hilbert space H4, where the initial state |O⟩ originates from the physical infinite-temperature initial state, while the final state ⟨I| corresponds to the trace operation in H2.
